title: A quantitative in vitro collagen uptake assay
author: Maassen, Warner, et al.

steps.title: Prepare FITC‑collagen coating
steps.instruction: Thaw an aliquot of FITC‑collagen (stock ~1 mg/mL, 10–200 µL per tube) on ice, keep on ice to prevent polymerisation. In a sterile laminar‑flow hood dilute the collagen to 10 µg/mL in sterile 1 X PBS (room temperature) by gently pipetting the total volume (e.g., 10 mL up and down twice with a 5 mL pipette).

steps.title: Apply collagen to culture vessels
steps.instruction: Add the diluted FITC‑collagen as follows: • Flow‑cytometry: 250–300 µL per well of a 24‑well plate. • Live‑cell imaging: 500–1000 µL to a CELLview glass‑bottom dish and swirl gently. • Immunofluorescence: sterilise 1½‑coverglass coverslips in 70 % ethanol for 15 min, transfer one coverslip to a well of a 24‑well plate, wash three times with sterile 1 X PBS at room temperature, then add 250–300 µL FITC‑collagen.

steps.title: Polymerise and wash collagen coat
steps.instruction: Cover the entire bottom of each well (or dish) with aluminium foil and incubate at room temperature for 1 h to allow polymerisation. Wash the wells twice with sterile 1 X PBS to remove excess/unpolymerised collagen. Keep the wells in sterile 1 X PBS at room temperature, protected from light, until cell seeding.

steps.title: Seed cells onto collagen
steps.instruction: Remove PBS from the coated surfaces. Add cell‑specific medium (for human monocyte‑derived macrophages: RPMI 1640 + 10 % FBS + 1 X L‑glutamine + optionally 1 X anti‑anti). Use 300–400 µL medium per 24‑well and 700–800 µL per CELLview dish. Add 1 × 10⁵ cells to each 24‑well (i.e., 100 µL of a 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL suspension) and 3–5 × 10⁵ cells to each CELLview dish. Incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to allow collagen uptake.

steps.title: Optional diluted collagen mix
steps.instruction: To reduce collagen thickness, on ice mix 400 µL cold rat‑tail collagen I (Thermo Fisher Gibco, Cat A1048301) with 125 µL water, 15 µL 1 M NaOH and 60 µL 10 × PBS. Add FITC‑collagen at a 1:100 molar ratio to this mixture before coating.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mM Trolox solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg Trolox in 860 µL methanol. Add 3077 µL H₂O (a precipitate forms), then add 63 µL 10 M NaOH; the solution becomes light‑yellow. Adjust to a final volume of 4 mL (100 mM).

steps.title: Live‑cell imaging preparation
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm phenol‑red‑free RPMI 1640 at 37 °C. After the 24 h incubation, inspect cells for viability. In a sterile hood aspirate the medium, wash once with 1 mL pre‑warmed phenol‑red‑free RPMI, and add 1 mL warm phenol‑red‑free RPMI. Keep the microscope stage and oil at 37 °C to minimise focus drift. Optionally image the collagen coat before further analysis.

steps.title: Fix cells for immunofluorescence
steps.instruction: Fix cells with 4 % (v/v) paraformaldehyde (EM grade, Aurion Cat 15710) for 15 min at 4 °C. Wash three times with sterile 1 X PBS. Samples may be stored in PBS at 4 °C until staining.

steps.title: Permeabilise and block
steps.instruction: Add 300–400 µL staining buffer (PBS containing 0.1 % w/v saponin; saponin must be present in all subsequent antibody steps) to each well and incubate at room temperature for 30 min to permeabilise.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Dilute primary antibodies in staining buffer with 0.1 % saponin to a final concentration of ~5 µg/mL (approximately 1:100–1:200 v/v). Add to samples and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Wash the samples three times with 1 X PBS to remove unbound primary antibody.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Dilute fluorescent secondary antibodies to 2.5 µg/mL in staining buffer with 0.1 % saponin (optionally add fluorescent phalloidin). Incubate at room temperature for 1 h.

steps.title: Final washes and mounting
steps.instruction: Wash three times with 1 X PBS. Place a 2.5 µL droplet of mounting media (70 % w/v Kaiser's glycerol gelatin, optionally containing 0.33 µg/mL DAPI) on a microscope slide, invert the coverslip onto the droplet, gently blot excess liquid with tissue, and leave in the dark for 1 h to cure. Seal the edges with nail polish and store at 4 °C (up to 2 weeks).

steps.title: Acquire immunofluorescence images
steps.instruction: Image the stained samples with a fluorescence microscope (e.g., Zeiss LSM800 confocal, 63× oil lens NA 1.4). For quantification, analyse particle number and size using the provided Fiji script that thresholds fluorescence automatically.

steps.title: Detach cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Remove medium from the 24‑well plate and wash twice with 1 X PBS. Add 200 µL Accutase (StemPro Accutase, Fisher Cat 11599686) to each well, swirl to cover the bottom, and incubate 10 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Verify cell rounding under a microscope. Pipette the Accutase with a P1000, shear to release cells, and transfer to a 96‑well V‑bottom plate. Centrifuge 300 × g for 3 min at 4 °C, decant supernatant, and vortex to resuspend the pellet in the residual 10–20 µL. Add 200 µL cold 1 X PBS to the original 24‑well, repeat the transfer, and pool all cells in the 96‑well plate. Discard the 24‑well plate.

steps.title: Viability staining and fixation
steps.instruction: Dilute Fixable Viability eFluor 780 (Thermo Fisher Cat 15383562) 1:1000 in cold PBS, vortex 10 s, and add 50–100 µL to each well. Incubate 15 min on ice (4 °C). Centrifuge 300 × g 3 min at 4 °C, decant, and vortex the pellet. Add 50–100 µL 4 % PFA, incubate 15 min at 4 °C. Wash twice by centrifugation (300 × g, 3 min, 4 °C) with 100–150 µL PBS each time, vortexing to resuspend the pellet after each wash. Finally resuspend cells in 100 µL PBS.

steps.title: Flow cytometry acquisition
steps.instruction: Acquire the samples on a plate‑format flow cytometer (e.g., CytoFlex S). Use forward‑ and side‑scatter gating to select single cells, exclude eFluor 780‑positive dead cells, and record FITC fluorescence to quantify collagen uptake. Include dynasore controls (0, 10, 100 µM) prepared from a 50 mM stock in anhydrous DMSO if desired.
